headline: Anthropic's $80B first-half loss signals AI infrastructure economics crisis
body: Anthropic reported an $80 billion net loss in the first half of 2026, driven primarily by massive computing infrastructure costs required to develop and deploy Claude at scale. This financial trajectory raises critical questions about the viability of current large language model economics, particularly for healthcare vendors considering AI integration into clinical workflows. Healthcare organizations evaluating AI partnerships need to scrutinize vendor sustainability and cost structures, as infrastructure burn rates directly impact product roadmaps, pricing models, and long-term availability. The broader implication: healthcare AI adoption timelines may slow as investors temper valuations and demand proof of profitability, forcing vendors to demonstrate clear ROI on clinical implementations rather than betting on speculative enterprise value.
